stem: During pretransplant infection-prevention teaching, which food-preparation precaution aligns with standard references?

options.text: Prevent cross-contamination between raw and cooked foods when preparing food
Use the same unwashed cutting board for raw poultry and ready-to-eat foods without separation
Cross-contamination precautions apply only to pediatric recipients
Immunosuppression eliminates the need for safe food-handling practices

explanation.rationale_correct: Dietary infection-prevention teaching includes preventing cross-contamination between raw and cooked foods during food preparation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Separating raw and cooked foods prevents cross-contamination rather than using shared unwashed surfaces.
rationale_incorrect.C: Food-safety precautions apply to immunosuppressed transplant recipients broadly.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppressed recipients remain at increased infection risk and require food-safety teaching.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → iii. Dietary precautions
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Prevent cross-contamination between raw and cooked foods when preparing food

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → iii. Dietary precautions (prevent cross-contamination between raw and cooked foods); PDF p. 116 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Cross-contamination angle distinct from dietary infection-prevention combo (cctc-1052) and unpasteurized-dairy teaching (cctc-1051); anchor verified on Cupples p. 116.

stem: A lung transplant candidate treated with antithymocyte globulin asks about posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) risk. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Potent immunosuppression such as polyclonal or monoclonal antilymphocyte therapy is a PTLD risk factor
Minimal immunosuppression is the only PTLD risk factor described
PTLD risk is unrelated to immunosuppression intensity
Antilymphocyte therapy eliminates all PTLD risk

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD risk factors include intense immunosuppression such as polyclonal antithymocyte globulin or monoclonal antibody therapy, along with Epstein-Barr virus mismatch and cytomegalovirus factors.

rationale_incorrect.B: Multiple risk factors beyond immunosuppression intensity are described, including viral mismatch.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppression intensity is a recognized PTLD risk factor.
rationale_incorrect.D: Potent immunosuppression increases rather than eliminates PTLD risk.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 2. Risk factors
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Intense immunosuppression: for example, polyclonal (antithymocyte globulin [Atgam]) or monoclonal antibody therapy

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 2.a. (intense immunosuppression including antithymocyte globulin); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Potent-immunosuppression PTLD risk angle distinct from EBV mismatch recall (cctc-2109) and CMV mismatch (cctc-2115); anchor verified on Cupples p. 281.

stem: When reviewing cytomegalovirus (CMV) serostatus during evaluation, which mismatch pattern is identified as a posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) risk factor?

options.text: Donor CMV seropositive and recipient CMV seronegative
Donor and recipient both CMV seronegative with no other factors
Recipient CMV seropositive status alone eliminates all PTLD risk
CMV serostatus has no relationship to PTLD risk

explanation.rationale_correct: CMV mismatch with a CMV-seropositive donor and CMV-seronegative recipient is listed among risk factors for PTLD, along with CMV disease and other immunosuppression-related factors.

rationale_incorrect.B: CMV donor-positive/recipient-negative mismatch is specifically identified as a risk factor.
rationale_incorrect.C: CMV factors contribute to risk rather than eliminating all PTLD risk alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: CMV mismatch and CMV disease are described PTLD risk factors.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → Epstein-Barr virus → 3. Risk factors for PTLD
primary_anchor.quote_hint: CMV mismatch (donor CMV seropositive; recipient CMV seronegative)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → Epstein-Barr virus → 3.d. (CMV D+/R− mismatch as PTLD risk factor); PDF p. 198 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. CMV-mismatch PTLD risk angle distinct from EBV D+/R− recall (cctc-2109) and CMV organ-specific combo (cctc-1072); anchor verified on Cupples p. 198.

stem: When explaining posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) treatment options during evaluation, which immunosuppression strategy aligns with standard references?

options.text: Switching to or adding an mTOR inhibitor such as sirolimus or everolimus for antineoplastic properties
Permanent intensification of calcineurin inhibitor therapy without evaluation
mTOR inhibitors are contraindicated in every PTLD case
PTLD is managed only with routine daily skin biopsy

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD treatment options include reduction or withdrawal of immunosuppression and switching to or adding an mTOR inhibitor because of the antineoplastic properties of sirolimus and everolimus.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppression is reduced or modified rather than intensified as initial PTLD management.
rationale_incorrect.C: mTOR inhibitors are treatment options rather than being universally contraindicated.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression modification and targeted therapies are primary approaches rather than skin biopsy alone.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 4. Treatment options
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Switching to or adding an mTOR inhibitor due the antineoplastic properties of mTOR inhibitors (sirolimus [Rapamune], everolimus [Zortress])

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 4.b. (mTOR inhibitor antineoplastic therapy); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
